Under President Donald J. Trump’s leadership, the U.S. Army this morning safely destroyed nearly five tons of degraded explosives at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant. All initial indications show the controlled detonation to be highly successful, with EPA monitors reporting zero detection of airborne lead and no secondary explosions or infrastructure damage.

This is what happens when competence runs the government. Handed a dangerous mess the Obama Administration left behind, the Trump Administration acted decisively, marshaling a whole-of-government approach that involved meticulous planning, pre-positioning hundreds of on-the-ground personnel, mitigation engineering, and real-time data collection to protect the safety, health, and wellbeing of nearby residents and livestock at every step.

Experts remain on the ground to coordinate community health assessments, answer questions, and provide ongoing support. Real-time air sampling and monitoring data can be viewed as it becomes available at epa.gov/iowadata.

Here’s what they’re saying:

  • President Donald J. Trump: “Early reports from Iowa are that the Army’s mitigation efforts have far exceeded expectations.”
  • Vice President JD Vance: “Credit to our great Chief of Staff Stephen Miller whose leadership was instrumental in making tough decisions and averting potential disaster. Where other administrations failed to act, President Trump confronted the task at hand. No one passed the buck. This team stepped up and protected the great people of Iowa.”
  • White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller: “President Trump has assembled the most exemplary team of leaders and patriots we have ever seen. I want to express my congratulations to Secretary Hegseth, the United States Army, and the entire stellar federal interagency… for flawlessly executing the controlled demolition of the explosive materials improperly placed and stored by the Obama Administration in Iowa in 2009… A tremendous display of unity of effort, purpose and action led by President Trump.”
  • Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency Lee Zeldin: “Over five hours after the Army’s controlled detonation of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa, all EPA air monitors continue to report a ZERO DETECT of airborne lead. As one way to put this morning’s controlled detonation into perspective, I have been informed that the release of particulate matter from Kansas City’s fireworks show at FIFA World Cup FanFest was roughly 10x greater than this morning’s detonation. After collecting 1,200 land, air, dust, and water samples before the detonation, 300 EPA personnel and contractors were pre-positioned for continued sampling during and after the detonation. They are now back in the field sampling air, land, and water. We will continue our work over the coming days and keep providing updates to the public as we get more information.”
  • Secretary of War Pete Hegseth: “Tremendous leadership by @POTUS and Chief of Staff Stephen Miller — and incredible execution by the @USArmy & entire interagency.  Thank you to everyone, and God bless Iowa.”
  • Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle: “The Army’s controlled, mitigated detonation exceeded all expectations and was a HUGE success. The threat of an uncontrolled spontaneous detonation has been eliminated. I am so proud of our SOLDIERS for their courage, training, mitigation, and precision! They put it on the line for all of us just like this every day! Thank you to President Trump and his administration for mobilizing an unprecedented whole of government approach to fix this problem once and for all for the great people of Iowa. We are watching EPA’s MASSIVE sensor array throughout the area closely, and there are no readings so far above 0.0. To the people of Iowa, we are with you all the way.”
  • Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. Kennedy, Jr.: “Today’s controlled detonation at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant demonstrates the power of a coordinated, whole-of-government response. Initial assessments indicate that measures to contain the blast and limit the spread of lead dust exceeded expectations, and real-time air monitors are reporting no detectable airborne lead. I thank President Trump and White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller for their leadership in coordinating federal resources to protect surrounding communities… Our responsibility does not end with the detonation. We will continue working with Iowa officials and our federal partners to assess potential health risks, share findings, and respond to residents’ needs. Iowa families deserve clear answers about what the monitoring shows, what remains under investigation, and what they should do to protect their health.”
  • Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins: “The U.S. Army successfully carried out the controlled detonation in Middletown, Iowa, this morning, with mitigation efforts exceeding expectations and showing zero initial detections of airborne lead. Our priority remains the safety of every Iowan affected. USDA is on the ground, and we’ll bring every resource we can to help our farmers and ranchers. To the families and producers worried about your homes, your livestock, and your livelihoods, I hear you. More than 140 USDA offices within 100 miles of Middletown will remain open to help. Our team will be here in the days and weeks ahead to answer your questions, help you access USDA resources, and assist with filing claims with the Army.”
  • Secretary of Energy Chris Wright: “@ENERGY’s world-class scientists and experts worked closely with federal partners to support today’s controlled detonation at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant by the @USArmy. @SandiaLabs provided critical foam suppression technology, while @Livermore_Lab contributed advanced atmospheric modeling. Their combined expertise helped inform and implement mitigation measures to protect the American people. Under the coordination of @StephenM, federal agencies united the full capabilities and expertise of the Trump Administration to prioritize the safety and security of all Americans.”
  • U.S. Army Sustainment Command Commanding General Maj. Gen. Eric Shirley: “I would characterize the controlled detonation as exceeding expectations… Every indication is that all of the [mitigations] that were employed absolutely reduced the lead azide threat. As we saw in the immediate aftermath through overhead coverage, all of the lead azide barrels were definitively removed. There was no secondary explosions. There was no kickout. There was no infrastructure damage in or around our installation.”
  • Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency Cameron Hamilton: “We believe that is a successful detonation… The elements which were ultimately connected to explosives and set for a time charge, we believe that they fully ignited — so that’s a fully and complete successful detonation… This really was a tremendous success, and I want to thank the President, I want to thank the Army, I want to thank just the tremendous interagency support for this effort.”
  • Director of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives Robert Cekada: “President Trump and Chief of Staff Miller ensured that we had every available tool and every available asset in the federal government to make sure that the mitigation efforts brought forth tools and equipment that we would never have been able to use in the years past. I absolutely can confirm that those mitigation efforts and the design plan laid out by the EOD personnel ensured that the blast drove the explosion into the ground and followed a blast channel that was designed to go down the right path to minimize any sort of dispersion of lead into the atmosphere 100% as planned. So, from the interagency perspective, none of this would have been possible without the tremendous leadership of President Trump, Chief of Staff Miller, and the entire federal interagency community.”
  • Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Dr. Erica Schwartz: “I’ve seen firsthand here in Iowa the extraordinary commitment of @CDCgov and ATSDR teams working alongside our state and federal partners to protect communities. Readiness isn’t just about responding when a crisis begins—it’s about staying committed through everything that follows. CDC will continue supporting this response for as long as Iowa and our partners need us.”
  • Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds: “I want to commend Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle, Army leadership, and the skilled soldiers who planned and executed a flawless detonation this morning at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant and express my gratitude to the Trump Administration for its whole-of-government response… This is a best-case scenario for the residents of Middletown and its surrounding communities.”
  • Missouri Gov. Mike Kehoe: “Since learning of the planned operation in Iowa, we have remained in communication with the @WhiteHouse, @SecArmy, @fema, @EPAregion7, @ATFHQ, @CDCgov, @USDA, and Iowa officials. It is because of the coordination of these agencies and their shared efforts to mitigate risk that today’s necessary detonation kept Americans safe. I especially want to thank the brave personnel of the @USArmy for their work to protect public health and safety.”
  • Sen. Chuck Grassley: “the hard work that went into this morning’s controlled detonation of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant shld not be understated Many local leaders hv been working around the clock w their federal partners to mitigate impact on surrounding communities as much as possible… The outcomes of the extensive mitigation efforts exceeded expectations 0.0 readings so far in the air & we will know soon the water/soil readings It appears the lead was contained to the greatest extent possible Monitoring levels will continue & must be transparent for public”
  • Iowa Secretary of Agriculture Mike Naig: “We appreciate the U.S. Army’s efforts to implement additional mitigation measures to contain the detonation and protect the residents, livestock, food and feed supplies in Middletown and the surrounding area. I also want to thank Secretary Rollins and her team at USDA for their work to support Iowa farmers… EPA’s real-time air monitors are not detecting airborne lead in the region so we believe the detonation was successfully contained. Based on information currently available, we don’t anticipate the detonation will have any negative impact on livestock health or food safety.”
  • Middletown (IA) Mayor Rodney Johnson: “We did not feel anything. We did not see anything.”
  • Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives: “Today’s operation in Iowa reflects what can be accomplished when government agencies work together. ATF was proud to stand alongside our federal, state, and local partners during today’s planned detonation, demonstrating our shared commitment to the communities we serve.”
  • Environmental Protection Agency Heartland Region: “EPA continues to closely monitor for any possible lead levels in the air following this morning’s controlled detonation of lead azide in Middletown, IA. At this point, ALL EPA real-time air monitors continue to report ZERO detection of airborne lead throughout the region… We pre-positioned 300 EPA employees and contractors, as well as robust equipment capabilities, to collect data as quickly and accurately as possible following this morning’s controlled detonation. Prior to the event, we collected 1,200 air, land, dust, and water samples to be further prepared to confirm any changes in levels compared to pre-detonation. We are working closely with our federal partners, including @USArmy, @fema, @HHSGov, @USDA to ensure any and all action is being taken to protect human health and the environment.”
  • National Weather Service: “The mitigation efforts in Iowa were a historic success — truly a remarkable achievement. In support of the @USArmy mission to safely clear hazardous material in Iowa, the NWS worked closely with partners to provide the atmospheric expertise needed to keep Americans safe as part of our public safety and national security mission. Our forecasters delivered detailed briefings, deployed to emergency operations centers, issued hourly forecasts, and launched weather balloons nearly every hour to make sure conditions stayed optimal and the public stayed safe. NWS thanks our dedicated forecasters and our federal, state, and local partners for this unprecedented interagency collaboration.”
  • U.S. Army: “Today’s successfully controlled detonation exceeded expectations. Credit goes to our EOD professionals and the Soldiers on the ground today, with every indication showing the munitions used substantially reduced the lead azide threat and safely addressed the hazard. There is a reading of 0.0 lead detected on the ground. Immediate overhead coverage after the operation confirmed that everything targeted for removal was cleared, with no secondary explosions, no kickout, and no infrastructure damage on or around the installation. Monitoring and verification remain front and center as teams wrap up post-event checks.”
